assessment.intent: Guide an accounting firm through choosing client fit, structuring service pages, handling sensitive enquiries and planning budget before hiring a designer.
assessment.specificity: Specific enough to separate personal tax, bookkeeping and advisory buyers, with concrete page, form, team, process and local-search recommendations.
assessment.evidence: Uses the BC OIPC privacy guidance and W3C forms guidance for the two sensitive claims; the rest is explicitly framed as practical design judgement rather than measured uplift.
assessment.voice: Sounds like Michael: connected conversational prose, thoughtful tradeoffs, Canadian spelling, no corporate padding and no invented client stories.
assessment.usefulAsset: A useful private planning asset that could help an accountant write a focused website brief and avoid collecting the wrong information publicly.
